lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: You picked one thing. Let me read you.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: A. The first-aid kit. You plan for damage before it happens.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: Under stress, you go protector mode. Fix it first. Feel it later.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: B. Food and water. Pure problem-solver. Your brain turns fear into a checklist.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: C. The radio. You don't survive alone. When you're scared, you reach for people.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Psychologists call it tend and befriend. Under stress, many of us look for connection, not escape.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: D. The photo. You protect meaning. You'd rather lose comfort than lose the reason.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: These are coping styles. Fix the problem, or protect the feeling. Both keep people going.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: None of them is wrong. It's just your first instinct.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: But some of you didn't pick at all. You froze.
